name: Photosynthesis, Respiration & Nutrition

objectives.text: Name sunlight, water, air, and nutrients from the soil as things a plant needs to grow
Compare plants grown with and without light and describe how lack of light changes their color and growth
Explain simply how a plant uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make its own food and give off oxygen
Explain that plants take up mineral nutrients from the soil through their roots and that fertilizer adds these nutrients
Diagram the inputs and outputs of photosynthesis and cellular respiration
Explain how a plant breaks down the sugars it makes through respiration to release energy for growth and maintenance
Describe the main role of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium in plant growth
Interpret the guaranteed analysis on a fertilizer label to identify the percentage of nitrogen, phosphate, and potash
Explain the role of chlorophyll and the light-dependent and light-independent reactions in photosynthesis
Describe the photosynthesis pathway using its balanced chemical equation with reactants and products
Describe how light color, intensity, and duration each affect plant growth
Classify the essential plant nutrients as macronutrients, secondary nutrients, or micronutrients and distinguish mobile from immobile nutrients
Differentiate C3, C4, and CAM photosynthesis and relate each type to common crops and their growing environments
Analyze how leaves capture light energy and exchange carbon dioxide, oxygen, and water vapor through stomata
Analyze how limiting factors such as light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature, and water affect the rate of photosynthesis
Analyze plant responses to light color, intensity, and duration including photoperiodic flowering in short-day and long-day crops
Explain how soil and growing media pH affects the availability of plant nutrients
Diagnose nutrient deficiency and toxicity symptoms in crops using visual symptoms along with soil and tissue test results
Calculate fertilizer application rates from a soil test recommendation for a field crop or greenhouse SAE
Monitor and adjust the electrical conductivity and pH of a nutrient solution in a hydroponic production system
Evaluate how temperature, humidity, and atmosphere in storage facilities control respiration rates and extend the shelf life of harvested plant products
Recommend modifications to light quality, intensity, or photoperiod such as supplemental lighting or blackout curtains to achieve desired plant growth
Evaluate strategies growers use to optimize photosynthetic efficiency in crop and greenhouse production such as carbon dioxide enrichment and controlled environment technologies
Design a nutrient management plan for a crop or greenhouse enterprise that balances yield goals, cost, and environmental stewardship

changes: Fixed the confession error by leaving scripture and confessions as truly empty arrays with no blank entries. Kept all six original objectives, rewording three slightly. The grade 4 objective now includes oxygen release and the grade 12 objective names specific strategies. Added respiration objectives on how plants use sugars for energy and on postharvest storage. Added a light dimension covering light measurements, photoperiodism, and lighting recommendations. Added C3, C4, and CAM differentiation and leaf gas exchange. Added a nutrition progression running from soil nutrients and NPK roles through fertilizer labels, nutrient classification, pH and availability, deficiency diagnosis, rate calculation, hydroponic solution management, and a capstone nutrient management plan. Standards are attached only where an objective directly teaches the candidate standard. Objectives below grade 9 and the nutrition objectives have no matching codes.
